readiness.mainReason: No blocking issue. The decision is answered early, the recommendation is specific and sequenced, and the key assumption is flagged and tested.
readiness.highestRiskIssue: The only open items are minor: an unconfirmed partner discount and an unstated basis for comparability.
readiness.whatCouldChangeIt: Nothing structural. Confirming the partner discount and the comparability basis would make it fully ready.

strengths.point: The answer is stated on the title slide and confirmed on slide 2, so a reader gets the decision immediately.
strengths.quote: Client E should launch a paid membership scheme, starting with a single tier in the autumn.

strengths.point: The headline number is marked as an assumption and a test is built around it, which is exactly the right instinct.
strengths.quote: The 8% assumption is conservative against the 32% attendance rate and is the main thing to test.

strengths.point: The first steps name an owner and a go or no-go trigger, so the plan is genuinely executable.
strengths.quote: Month three: full launch if the soft launch clears 5%.

findings.title: The partner discount is offered as a benefit without confirming partners have agreed.
findings.principle: Evidence grounding: do not promise what is not yet secured.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 7 lists a discount with local partners as a member benefit. The deck does not say whether partners have agreed or what the discount is.
findings.why: Advertising an unsecured benefit risks a member promise Client E cannot keep.
findings.reflect: Which partners have confirmed, and what exactly have they agreed to.
findings.fix: Confirm the partner terms before listing the benefit, or mark it as planned rather than confirmed.

findings.title: The comparable groups are asserted as comparable without saying on what basis.
findings.principle: Evidence relevance: show why a benchmark applies.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 5 cites three comparable arts non-profits charging 40 to 60 pounds without stating the basis for comparability such as size, art form or area.

evidence.quote: Three comparable local arts non-profits run membership at 40 to 60 pounds a year

findings.why: A benchmark only informs the price if the comparators genuinely resemble Client E.
findings.reflect: On what dimension are these three groups comparable to Client E.
findings.fix: Add one line on why these three are the right comparators, or note the limitation.

questionsForLead: Have any local partners actually agreed to the member discount yet.
Is the mailing list clean enough that 1,400 is a real reachable base.

learningNote.lesson: A strong recommendation states its assumption and builds a cheap test around it, rather than hiding the uncertainty.
learningNote.weakHabit: None material here. The habit to keep is marking the load-bearing assumption and testing it before scaling.
learningNote.exercise: Before the full launch, write down what conversion result would make you stop, not just what would make you go. Deciding the stop rule in advance is what keeps a pilot honest.

notAssessed: Whether the 8% conversion assumption will hold in practice. That is what the soft launch tests.
Whether local partners will agree to a discount. Not yet confirmed in the deck.
